check_text:
protocol.py: 2 biology problems (1 error, 1 note).

1. ERROR SOURCE-TOO-SHALLOW: The pipette draws air from well A1 in slot 4: the liquid is
below the tip
   line 78:  p20.mix(5, 16, dest_well)
   At line 78 the p20_single_gen2 draws 16 ul from well A1 in slot 4 with its tip 1 mm above
   the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 20 ul, which in this NEST 96 Well Plate
   200 µL Flat reaches only 0.63 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air (this line
   did it 240 times; 3,840 ul of air in all). The simulator does not notice: it does not
   follow the liquid. These are mixing strokes: the tip stirs air, and the well is not
   mixed. Source wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 40 more in slot 4.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 40 more in slot 4.
   Fix: Mix lower, with `well.bottom(0.5)`, so the tip is in the liquid. This well needs
   about 35 ul in it for the surface to reach 1 mm.
   Source: Opentrons: liquid control (aspirates 1 mm above the bottom of the well by
   default)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/basic_commands/liquids.html
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Gilson guide to pipetting (immersion depth 2 to 3 mm for 1 to 100 ul)
           https://solutions.pipette.com/wp-content/uploads/Gilson-Guide-to-Pipetting.pdf
   Source: labautomation.io 7592: negative controls positive after aspirating air
           https://labautomation.io/t/aspiration-dispense-liquid-class-incompatibity/7592
   Source: Integra: 260 ul dead volume in a standard reservoir
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/minimizing-dead-volume-during-qpcr-set-divided-reservoir-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   [9dbd52ab02d1]

2. NOTE CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 48 stocks
   line 74:  p20.aspirate(lib_vol, src_well)
   At line 74 the tip went into library 1 (well A1 in slot 2), library 2 (well A2 in slot
   2), library 3 (well A3 in slot 2), library 4 (well A4 in slot 2) and 44 more while it
   still carried buffer (well A1 in slot 3) from an earlier step (this line did it 48
   times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it
   touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. The protocol does
   not draw from them again, so this run is not harmed, but what is left in the stock is no
   longer clean for the next run.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 40 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 74 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [29ca01d9356e]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

findings.title: The pipette draws air from well A1 in slot 4: the liquid is below the tip
findings.explanation: At line 78 the p20_single_gen2 draws 16 ul from well A1 in slot 4 with its tip 1 mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 20 ul, which in this NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat reaches only 0.63 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air (this line did it 240 times; 3,840 ul of air in all). The simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. These are mixing strokes: the tip stirs air, and the well is not mixed. Source wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 40 more in slot 4.
findings.fix: Mix lower, with `well.bottom(0.5)`, so the tip is in the liquid. This well needs about 35 ul in it for the surface to reach 1 mm.

findings.title: A used tip went into a stock: 48 stocks
findings.explanation: At line 74 the tip went into library 1 (well A1 in slot 2), library 2 (well A2 in slot 2), library 3 (well A3 in slot 2), library 4 (well A4 in slot 2) and 44 more while it still carried buffer (well A1 in slot 3) from an earlier step (this line did it 48 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. The protocol does not draw from them again, so this run is not harmed, but what is left in the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
findings.fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 74 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids afterwards with a fresh tip each.
